items.what: Tracker's JourneyDistance projects the player onto each leg's points to get yards remaining (Tracker.lua:129-148), a third copy of ns.OnWalk (Journey.lua:295-317; canonical) and Arrow.lua:109-120.
items.why: Differences: Tracker caches per-leg lengths/after (intentional, avoids recomputation per tick), has no off-path reach limit, applies it to active boat/flight legs as well as walks, and adds the off-path distance only for walks (intentional). The projection/after arithmetic itself is identical and would need the same fix in each copy; OnWalk could take precomputed lengths, or expose the projection as a shared helper.
items.reason: These serve different contracts: Tracker caches discontinuous, multimodal geometry, excludes jumps and continent gaps, and adds off-path distance only for walks; tests/tracker_ui.lua:98–106 requires those exclusions, and executing the unchanged functions produced 200 yards versus OnWalk’s 1000 for the jump fixture. OnWalk instead supplies reach-limited walking progress, while Arrow selects a bend without calculating remaining yards; the shared clamped projection is a small mathematical idiom, covered by the lens’s exclusions.

items.what: The `.default == true` clauses (lines 77, 79, 80, 84, 85) assert a value the spec itself supplies: its ns.Defaults stub (lines 55-59, a hand copy of Core.lua DEFAULTS described as 'every row on except the compass') returns true for every key but compass.
items.why: Changing a default in Core.lua DEFAULTS (the single source per the project conventions) cannot fail these asserts, and neither could Settings.lua hardcoding true instead of reading ns.Defaults[key], since the stub answers true for everything. The key/order/tooltip/callback checks in the same lines are real and stay. A meaningful check would give the stub distinct per-key values (or read Core.lua's table) and assert Settings forwards them.
items.reason: In-memory LuaJIT mutation testing passed the baseline but failed tests/settings_spec.lua:79 when Settings.lua forwarded ns.db[key] instead of ns.Defaults[key] for guideStops, demonstrating coverage of a realistic reset-default regression. Hardcoded true remains a coverage gap, but these assertions exercise production forwarding and fall under the lens’s thin-test exception.

items.quote: Run("stale dock cluster tooltip", function()
items.what: The stale-dock-cluster regression (docks 999998/999999 with no departures, then ns.AddDockTooltip) is also the whole of tests/docktooltip_spec.lua:27-33, which additionally checks DockVisits and a kinds-less cluster. The dedicated spec is the canonical home; the smoke copy is a subset.
items.why: Same fixture ids, same kinds table, same assertion on DockDepartures, same call; docktooltip_spec's header says it exists to pin this crash. Both run in the spec loop, so a fixture change (e.g. the ids becoming real docks) must be made twice. Difference: smoke's cluster docks lack x/y; not a deliberate variant as far as the comments say.

items.quote: Run(label .. " refresh surfaces", function()
items.what: The list of surfaces to re-render (ns.RefreshTracker/RefreshMap/RefreshMinimapPins/RefreshCompass/RefreshRouteButton, plus the compass/route-button stat counting) is written three times in the file: DrivePrime (smoke_spec.lua:506-519), DrivePaths 'refresh surfaces' (531-546) and the per-profile 're-render' (729-736). A new surface added to the sweep has to be added in each.
items.why: The copies have already drifted: 'refresh surfaces' adds RefreshTaxiRoute and RefreshGuideStops, 're-render' omits the stat counting and ticks 0.2 s instead of Flush. No comment says the differences are intended; one local RefreshSurfaces() would serve all three.

items.quote: Run(label .. " final", function() end)
items.what: A no-op Run that can never fail: the empty function adds no errors after `before` is captured, so all it does is add 1 per profile to the reported `checks` count.
items.why: Run (smoke_spec.lua:58-73) records a failure only when fn throws or #errors grows during fn; an empty fn does neither. Errors from earlier steps are already attributed by their own Run calls.
